$comment: Presenter rig contract. This file is the ONLY place that knows how a given
character asset is put together. Swapping in a different Lottie presenter
should mean editing this file - not the renderer and not any lesson data.
production/scripts/build_presenter_lottie.py reads this to decide how to bake
per-scene animation. src/presenter/Presenter.tsx reads nothing from here at
render time: lip-sync is resolved at BUILD time by design (deterministic, and
far cheaper than solving visemes per frame).

act-presenter-v1.label: ACT presenter (current, approved in Lesson 1)
$comment_kind: single-file  = one Lottie holding the whole character; actions are
expressed by re-timing its own layers (what we do today).
action-clips = a folder of one Lottie per action (idle/talking/point-left
...). Set kind to this and fill `clips` when a professional
asset arrives. The builder picks the clip named by the
scene's presenter.action and injects visemes into it.

$comment_mode: viseme-layers  = the asset already contains one drawn mouth per viseme.
Preferred. Map them in `viseme_layers` and the builder
derived-shapes = the asset has too few mouths (ours has 3), so we derive
a full set by scaling its widest mouth. Current approach.
none           = no usable mouth. Builder falls back to the asset's own
talking loop. NEVER fall back to volume-based faking.
$comment_jaw: jaw_drop_factor: how much extra vertical drop a taller viseme gets, on
top of its own scale - a taller mouth drops the jaw rather than just
jaw_bias (0-1): how much of that vertical change/offset an UPPER-lip
vertex receives relative to a lower one. Low = upper lip stays almost
fixed and the lower lip/jaw does the opening, like a real mouth.
corner_pull (0-1+): extra horizontal scale at the mouth's corners
versus its centreline, so a wide viseme visibly pulls the corners and a
round one visibly pinches them, instead of every viseme looking like
the same shape at a different size.

eyes.$comment: Source blink is a DOUBLE blink (~0.48s, two closures) which flickers when re-timed. Re-authored as one human blink.

brows.$comment: Source twitch is 0.6s with an overshoot - reads as nervous. Slowed and softened.

actions.$comment: Vocabulary a scene may request. This character has no arms, so gestures resolve to a head lean; a rigged asset can map these to real clips.
